items.usage: Move to clearance or approach position at rapid rate without cutting.
items.notes: Axes move independently at their own rapid rates, so the path may not be a straight line. Verify clearance. Fanuc lathe default plane is XZ (G18).

items.usage: Cut a straight line at the programmed feed rate.
items.notes: Feed meaning depends on active feed mode (G98 per-min / G99 per-rev).

items.params: X Z I K or R
items.usage: Cut a clockwise arc in the active turning plane.
items.notes: Arc direction viewed in the active plane. I/K (incremental from start) or R radius; full-circle support varies by control.

items.params: X Z I K or R
items.usage: Cut a counterclockwise arc in the active turning plane.
items.notes: Companion to G02; same I/K/R rules.

items.usage: Pause the program for a set time (e.g. for chamfer breaking or threading exit).
items.notes: P is milliseconds on Fanuc; X is seconds. Check your control's unit.

items.usage: Write offset / parameter data from the program (tool or work offset sets).
items.notes: Format is control- and option-specific. Verify before use.

items.usage: Sets the normal turning plane for arcs and canned cycles.
items.notes: Default plane on a standard two-axis Fanuc lathe.

items.usage: Program coordinates in inches.
items.notes: Sets input units; does not convert existing coordinates.

items.usage: Program coordinates in millimetres.
items.notes: Sets input units; does not convert existing coordinates.

items.params: U W or X Z (intermediate point)
items.usage: Return axis(es) to machine reference, passing through the programmed intermediate point.
items.notes: Coordinates on the G28 block create an intermediate move. Not automatically a safe retract — verify path.

items.usage: Single-pass thread cut synchronized to spindle (like G01 with spindle sync).
items.notes: Basic threading; G76 is the usual multi-pass cycle. Spindle must be in CSS or fixed RPM with sync enabled.

items.usage: Cancel active tool-nose radius compensation before a safe exit or tool change.
items.notes: Use a deliberate lead-out clear of the part before/while canceling.

items.usage: Offset the tool to the left of the programmed path by the nose radius.
items.notes: Requires a tool-nose-radius / orientation (TNR) setting in the offset page.

items.usage: Offset the tool to the right of the programmed path by the nose radius.
items.notes: Requires a tool-nose-radius / orientation (TNR) setting in the offset page.

items.description: Max spindle speed clamp / coordinate set (control-dependent)
items.usage: Commonly clamps maximum RPM when using constant surface speed (G96).
items.notes: G50 meaning varies by control (some use it for coordinate system setting). Verify the machine manual.

items.usage: Select stored G54 work offset as programmed part-zero.
items.notes: G54–G59 are the six standard work offsets. Each selects stored values; none measure or set part zero.

items.usage: Select stored G55 work offset.
items.notes: Second of the G54–G59 work offsets.

items.usage: Select stored G56 work offset.
items.notes: Third of the G54–G59 work offsets.

items.usage: Select stored G57 work offset.
items.notes: Fourth of the G54–G59 work offsets.

items.usage: Select stored G58 work offset.
items.notes: Fifth of the G54–G59 work offsets.

items.usage: Select stored G59 work offset.
items.notes: Sixth of the G54–G59 work offsets.

items.usage: Finish a profile previously defined by sequence blocks (after G71/G72/G73).
items.notes: P/Q mark the start/end sequence numbers of the profile definition.

items.params: U R P Q W F (format varies)
items.usage: Rough OD/ID turning in repeated passes along a defined profile.
items.notes: One-line and two-line formats differ by control generation. Match your control exactly.

items.params: W R P Q U F (format varies)
items.usage: Rough facing in repeated passes across a defined profile.
items.notes: Parameter letters and cycle format vary by control.

items.params: U W R P Q (format varies)
items.usage: Roughing that follows an existing shape (e.g. castings/forgings) rather than straight stock.
items.notes: Removes material in a repeating pattern offset from the finished profile.

items.usage: Peck drilling axially from the face; also used for face grooving on some controls.
items.notes: Especially control-specific. Verify the manual before use.

items.params: R X Z P Q F (format varies)
items.usage: Grooving with repeated pecks on OD or ID.
items.notes: Cycle meaning and parameter format vary by control.

items.params: P Q R X Z F (format varies)
items.usage: Cuts a thread over multiple controlled passes (the usual threading cycle).
items.notes: One-line and two-line formats differ significantly by control generation. Match your control exactly.

items.usage: Simple straight cutting cycle for OD or ID.
items.notes: On some controls G90 is absolute programming; on lathe canned-cycle use it is the cutting cycle. Control-dependent.

items.usage: Cut a thread in repeated passes to a defined end point.
items.notes: On some controls G92 is coordinate setting; on lathe canned-cycle use it is the thread cycle. Control-dependent.

items.usage: Simple facing cycle cutting perpendicular to the spindle axis.
items.notes: On some controls G94 is feed-per-minute; on lathe canned-cycle use it is the facing cycle. Control-dependent.

items.usage: Spindle RPM auto-adjusts to keep a constant cutting speed as diameter changes.
items.notes: Pair with a max-RPM clamp (often G50 S...) so RPM cannot run away at small diameters.

items.usage: Run spindle at a fixed commanded RPM (cancels CSS).
items.notes: Use when a fixed RPM is required by the process.

items.usage: Set feed mode to inches/mm per minute.
items.notes: On Fanuc lathes G98 = per-minute, G99 = per-revolution. (Some other controls swap these — verify.)

items.usage: Set feed mode to inches/mm per spindle revolution.
items.notes: On Fanuc lathes G99 = per-revolution (the common lathe default). Verify your control.
